title: bug: postflight-worktree.cjs serena-ignore and serena-ignore-wt fail on moe/work-2026-10-24 bd75f88a (both wrappers), because e575ecec (task-3ef33217) made moe-serena-ignore.mjs write an ignored_memory_patterns block but did not update the harness's expected serenaBlock, so postflight.sh and postflight.ps1 both throw at the worktree suite
description: Repro: `git archive bd75f88a scripts` into /mnt/d/moe-scratch/x, then `MOE_WORKTREE_ONLY=serena-ignore,serena-ignore-wt node scripts/tests/postflight-worktree.cjs sh <x>/scripts/moe-agent.sh <x>/scripts/tests/postflight-fake-proxy.js <x>/tmp $(command -v bash)` -> both FAILED. The diff is that `actual` has two extra comment lines ('# Moe also hides QA-archived memories (_archive/.*)...') and an 'ignored_memory_patterns: ["_archive/.*"]' block that serenaBlock() at postflight-worktree.cjs:1763 lacks. The ps1 leg (powershell.exe 5.1 and pwsh 7) fails identically, and postflight.ps1:1245 then throws, so every later section (accounts, the vm-route suite, ...) never runs. Origin is task-3ef3321758f94dad89875a5b64792e12 (epic-be924fb8). Found by worker-a408f113 while gating task-62ec51f1 on the merged tree. Fix it in the harness's expected block, or in the script if the block is wrong.
definitionOfDone: MOE_WORKTREE_ONLY=serena-ignore,serena-ignore-off,serena-ignore-wt passes for postflight-worktree.cjs on both sh and ps1 at the fix's commit.
Full bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh and postflight.ps1 (5.1) get past the worktree suite with no FAILED line.

implementationPlan.description:
Edit scripts/tests/postflight-worktree.cjs only, with the Edit tool (TOOL witness). Never touch scripts/moe-serena-ignore.mjs or scripts/tests/serena-ignore.test.mjs.
In `serenaBlock` (:1809-1814), add the two things scripts/moe-serena-ignore.mjs has rendered since e575ecec (task-3ef33217). Keep the expectation a LITERAL, as serena-ignore.test.mjs's EXPECTED does. Never import renderBlock: the harness would then follow any regression in the script.
(a) After `'# yourself outside this block; Moe then removes this block.',` add the two new WHY lines, before `'ignore_all_files_in_gitignore: false'`:
`'# Moe also hides QA-archived memories (_archive/.*); set ignored_memory_patterns yourself outside',`
`'# this block to keep your own list instead.',`
(b) After `...pats.map(x=>`  - "${x}"`),` add `'ignored_memory_patterns:','  - "_archive/.*"',` before `'# <<< moe serena-ignore <<<'`.
The resulting array is: BEGIN, the 6 WHY lines, 'ignore_all_files_in_gitignore: false', 'ignored_paths:', the pats items, 'ignored_memory_patterns:', '  - "_archive/.*"', END, ''. That is renderBlock's order (moe-serena-ignore.mjs:142).
Why `_archive/.*` alone: the fixture's project.yml, in the control and in W's WT-06 copy, has no ignored_memory_patterns, so the script's list is project.yml's own (none) plus `_archive/.*`. That holds for both files.
The MOE_SERENA_IGNORE_ pattern counts (8 and 9) count ignored_paths only, so they stay as they are.
Add one line to the comment above SERENA_USER (:1803-1805) saying the block also carries ignored_memory_patterns (task-3ef33217). Change nothing else: not SERENA_PATS, the fixture, serena-ignore-off or any other case.
Quick check from the worktree root, which prints `[worktree] 3 ok, 0 failed`:
`F=$(mktemp -d /tmp/e45d-q.XXXXXX) && cp scripts/tests/postflight-fake-proxy.js $F/fp.js && env $(env | awk -F= '/^(MOE_|CLAUDE)/{printf "-u %s ", $1}') MOE_WORKTREE_ONLY=serena-ignore,serena-ignore-off,serena-ignore-wt node scripts/tests/postflight-worktree.cjs sh "$PWD/scripts/moe-agent.sh" $F/fp.js $F "$BASH"`
The architect ran the same check: HEAD gives serena-ignore and serena-ignore-wt FAILED, and this exact edit gives 3 ok on sh (15 s) and on PS 5.1 (32 s).
implementationPlan.note: serenaBlock now has the two WHY lines and ignored_memory_patterns; sh quick check 3 ok.

implementationPlan.description:
Gate (DoD 1 and DoD 2): run the two legs below from the ROOT of your task worktree, concurrently. Each must exit 0.
Leg A, WSL bash:
cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && E=$(env | awk -F= '/^(MOE_|CLAUDE)/{printf "-u %s ", $1}') && T=scripts/tests && F=$(mktemp -d /tmp/e45d-a.XXXXXX) && cp $T/postflight-fake-proxy.js $F/fp.js && env $E MOE_WORKTREE_ONLY=serena-ignore,serena-ignore-off,serena-ignore-wt node $T/postflight-worktree.cjs sh "$PWD/scripts/moe-agent.sh" $F/fp.js $F "$BASH" && { env $E bash $T/postflight.sh > $F/postflight.sh.log 2>&1; echo "postflight.sh exit=$? log=$F/postflight.sh.log"; } && grep -E '^\[worktree\] [0-9]+ ok, 0 failed$' $F/postflight.sh.log && ! grep -E '^\[worktree\] .* FAILED' $F/postflight.sh.log
Leg B, Windows PowerShell 5.1:
cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && N="/mnt/c/Program Files/nodejs/node.exe" && P=/mnt/c/Windows/System32/WindowsPowerShell/v1.0/powershell.exe && T=scripts/tests && S=$(mktemp -d /mnt/d/moe-scratch/e45d-b.XXXXXX) && w(){ wslpath -w "$1"; } && cp $T/postflight-fake-proxy.js $S/fp.js && MOE_WORKTREE_ONLY=serena-ignore,serena-ignore-off,serena-ignore-wt WSLENV=MOE_WORKTREE_ONLY "$N" "$(w $T/postflight-worktree.cjs)" ps1 "$(w scripts/moe-agent.ps1)" "$(w $S/fp.js)" "$(w $S)" powershell && { WSLENV= "$P" -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "$(w $T/postflight.ps1)" > $S/postflight.ps1.log 2>&1; echo "postflight.ps1 exit=$? log=$S/postflight.ps1.log"; } && grep -aE '^\[worktree\] [0-9]+ ok, 0 failed' $S/postflight.ps1.log && ! grep -aE '^\[worktree\] .* FAILED' $S/postflight.ps1.log
What each leg does: it runs the 3 targeted cases (DoD 1), then the FULL harness with its output in a log. It greps the worktree suite's summary for `0 failed` and checks there is no FAILED line (DoD 2).
Error handling:
- A leg fails closed when the targeted run or either grep fails.
- The harness's own exit code is printed, not used as the leg's status. DoD 2 asks only that the run gets past the worktree suite.
How to run:
- The fixtures for sh go under /tmp (mkfifo fails on /mnt/d). The ps1 fixtures go under /mnt/d/moe-scratch, because Windows cannot reach /tmp.
- Launch each leg DETACHED: a runner file in scratch whose FIRST line is `echo $$ > pid`, then the leg, then `echo EXIT=$?`. Poll with `timeout 570 bash -c 'until grep -q ^EXIT= <log>; do sleep 15; done'`, repeated (mem:convention-postflight-scratch-harness: `set -m; setsid … & echo $!` records the wrong PID).
- Expect leg A to take about 30-45 min and leg B (PS 5.1) about 45-55 min.
What to expect:
- At bc4793cf the full postflight.sh suite read `[worktree] 75 ok, 2 failed` (serena-ignore and serena-ignore-wt), after `PASS frozen candidate scenarios: 106`, `PASS owner guard scenarios: 16` and `PASS migration landing scenarios: 12`. Expect `77 ok, 0 failed` on sh.
- If a harness exits non-zero AFTER the worktree suite, that is not this change: those sections have not run in any gate since e575ecec landed (2026-11-04 08:23Z). Name the section and its first failing line in complete_task's summary and post it in #general for a new row. Do not fix it here.
- Under heavy load, set MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC=180 on the run, and say so.
Reporting:
- Use both legs joined with ' && ' as verification.command, exitCode 0 only when both legs exited 0, and each leg's last lines as outputTail.
- Kill only the PIDs you recorded. Never pattern-kill (shared-host rail). Delete your scratch dirs by literal path afterwards.

Adversarial self-review, then complete_task with step 2's evidence.
1. `git status --porcelain` and `git diff --stat` name only scripts/tests/postflight-worktree.cjs. The diff is the two WHY lines, the ignored_memory_patterns pair and the one comment line.
2. Cross-check the literal against the script in a scratch dir, never in the harness. Run a node one-off there that imports renderBlock from scripts/moe-serena-ignore.mjs and asserts that renderBlock([...SERENA_PATS,'src/**/*.tmp'], ['_archive/.*']) equals the edited serenaBlock for the same pats.
3. Mutant, in a scratch copy: drop the `'ignored_memory_patterns:','  - "_archive/.*"',` pair and re-run the targeted sh command. serena-ignore and serena-ignore-wt must FAIL again, which proves the expectation is load-bearing.
4. Think it through:
   - serena-ignore-off still asserts the file is untouched (SERENA_USER).
   - The block is LF on every engine, because node writes it.
   - A project.yml that carries its own memory list is covered by serena-ignore.test.mjs, not by this suite.
5. If anything changed, re-run both legs of step 2 and use the fresh output.

renderBlock(patterns, memoryPatterns) (moe-serena-ignore.mjs:142) writes BEGIN, WHY, 'ignore_all_files_in_gitignore: false', 'ignored_paths:' plus its items, then 'ignored_memory_patterns:' plus its items when memoryPatterns is non-null, then END and ''.

memoryPatterns(yml, user) (moe-serena-ignore.mjs:278) returns project.yml's own ignored_memory_patterns plus '_archive/.*'. Here that is ['_archive/.*'], since the fixture's project.yml has no such key. It returns null when project.local.yml sets the key outside the block.

postflight-worktree.cjs:1809-1814: serenaBlock lacks both additions. serenaIgnore (:1833) and serenaIgnoreWt (:1882) compare readOr() against it; serenaIgnoreOff (:1850) only checks that the file is untouched.
postflight.sh:1262 and postflight.ps1:1244-1245 run the suite and stop the harness on its non-zero exit.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Chosen: update the harness's literal expectation. The script's block is the intended, QA-approved behavior of task-3ef33217, and serena-ignore.test.mjs already pins the same text. Rejected: (1) importing renderBlock into the harness: it is tautological, and it needs a CJS-to-ESM dynamic import. (2) Changing the script: it is right. (3) Adding an end-to-end case for a project.yml that carries its own memory list: the serena-ignore.test.mjs U-cases cover it, and it is not this row's DoD.

Applying this exact edit to a scratch copy gave `3 ok, 0 failed` on sh (15 s) and on PS 5.1 via node.exe (32 s). A PS 5.1 probe showed that output redirected through WSL arrives as plain LF ASCII, so leg B's greps match. Sections after the worktree suite have not run in any gate since e575ecec (11-04 08:23Z), so a later failure there is unrelated; report it and do not fix it here.
